match.header: What can I do with Poppy — and why is it useful?

set.header: What can I do with Poppy — and why is it useful?
set.content:
Poppy gives a personal agent a standard way to identify itself and work within the access a business offers. For account tasks, the person approves the access and the business decides which actions are available.

  • Ask before account sign-in: read product facts, opening hours or published support guidance through a guest session.
  • Continue with permission: an account integration could offer returns, appointments or order changes, limited to the access the person approved.
  • Keep session context across supported channels: the protocol connects a website, APIs and a business’s own agent through a shared session model.
set.sidebar_content:
Try it in TYPO3 Lab

Our current profile reads two published explanations. It establishes and renews verified guest sessions and rejects reused request proofs.

The agent supplies an opaque guest user identifier. This identifies its guest session; it does not prove the person’s identity or sign them in to a customer account.

The playground tests the protocol without a language model. This release does not book appointments, change accounts or edit TYPO3.

set.bodytext:
Poppy gives personal agents a shared way to discover a website, identify themselves and work within the access the website offers. TYPO3 Lab implements the signed-out profile of draft 0.1: verified guest sessions and a read-only OpenAPI endpoint for published explanations.

Our first use case is simple: ask what the lab says about Poppy or Pi Durable and receive the CMS text with its source URL. A separate TYPO3 extension handles the protocol. Editors own the explanation in normal TYPO3 content records.

The Poppy API offers public knowledge through a verified guest session, with no Poppy customer-account sign-in or editing permissions. The lab’s own website login is separate. Poppy is an early draft, so we document the supported profile and test its security boundaries.

match.header: From discovery to a sourced answer

set.header: From discovery to a sourced answer
set.content: The registered agent reads the discovery document and checks the issuer. It proves its identity and establishes a guest session with separate client and user-session assertions. Each knowledge request carries the session token and a fresh DPoP proof. TYPO3 returns the published explanation with a link back to this page.

set.subheadline: Discovery, agent verification and a session token lead to a published answer with a source URL.

set.title: Discover
set.description: The personal agent reads /.well-known/poppy.json to learn the issuer and available API.

set.title: Identify
set.description: TYPO3 verifies the registered agent’s client assertion and its separate user-session assertion. The guest identifier is supplied by the agent; it does not establish a customer-account identity.

set.title: Start a guest session
set.description: The agent receives a short-lived session token bound to its DPoP key. A copied token alone is insufficient to call the knowledge API.

set.title: Ask the lab
set.description: The agent sends the session token and a fresh DPoP proof, selecting Poppy or Pi Durable. TYPO3 reads the published “What TYPO3 Lab says” section and returns its text and source.

set.title: Continue safely
set.description:
The agent renews the guest session with fresh client and user-session assertions when necessary. Reusing a request proof is rejected.

Run the flow in the playground and use “See the requests” to inspect the actual responses.

set.content:
Open the live Poppy playground. Ask about Poppy or Pi Durable, renew the guest session and test replay rejection. The answer comes from the published TYPO3 section “What TYPO3 Lab says”.

Inspect the live discovery document, OAuth server metadata and OpenAPI schema.

Discovery is public. Starting or renewing a guest session requires an administrator-registered personal agent, separate client and user-session assertions, and a fresh DPoP proof. Knowledge requests use the session token and a fresh DPoP proof.

match.term: Field guide and stable protocol URLs

set.term: Field guide and stable protocol URLs
set.definition: The field guide lives under /agent-nexus/poppy/. Protocol endpoints remain under /poppy, with discovery under /.well-known/. Moving the explanation does not change the issuer or require agent registration again.

set.content:
• Domain-wide HTTPS discovery and reciprocal OAuth issuer metadata.
  • ES256 and RS256 agent authentication, short-lived assertions and atomic replay rejection.
  • Guest sessions, renewal, random opaque Session Tokens and DPoP key binding.
  • A read-only OpenAPI endpoint for explicitly selected, published English CMS text.
  • Ordinary website browsing, separate from Poppy customer-account sign-in.
set.sidebar_content:
Outside this release

Direct, device and mediated account sign-in, Account Tokens, browser-session exchange, MCP and Poppy conversations are not advertised by discovery.

Existing TYPO3 MCP credentials do not become Poppy credentials.

See the official draft specification and Sierra’s draft announcement of 9 October 2026.

set.title: Poppy
set.content:
Identify the personal agent and establish a session for permitted access. MCP exposes tools; OpenAPI describes HTTP operations. This profile uses a read-only OpenAPI channel.

Agent Nexus brings these six protocols together: five demos from Agent Nexus and this independent Poppy extension.

Personal agents often have to sign in as their person and click through pages built for humans. Poppy proposes a standard way for a business to recognise the agent, associate its session with a person and control the actions available.

The person decides how much account access to approve. The business decides which actions it supports. A company can serve agents through its website, APIs or an agent of its own.
set.sidebar_content:
From announcement to draft

Sierra announced the Personal Agent Protocol on 6 October 2026 with Meta, Genesys, Instinct, NiCE, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart.

On 9 October 2026, Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor published the first draft, nicknamed Poppy. Sierra reported 35 additional design partners, including Adyen, Bank of America, Cloudflare, Mastercard, OpenAI, PayPal, Target, Visa and Zapier.

set.subheadline: The draft describes a broader protocol. This lab implements its guest-session profile and one read-only API.

set.title: Discovery
set.description:
A company publishes /.well-known/poppy.json to describe its issuer, interaction channels and supported sign-in methods.

In the lab: implemented. Open the discovery document.

set.title: Sessions
set.description:
An agent identifies itself and establishes a session for its person. A guest session can already support questions about stock levels or a returns policy.

In the lab: verified guest sessions with renewal and an opaque, agent-supplied guest identifier.

set.title: Account sign-in
set.description:
For account tasks, the person signs in through a business-controlled OAuth flow and approves the access. The business can issue an Account Token for that access.

In the lab: outside this release.

set.title: Session context across channels
set.description:
Supported website, API and conversational channels can retain session context before and after account sign-in. Browser access uses a separate session-exchange mechanism; a session token is not simply reused as a browser cookie.

In the lab: one read-only OpenAPI channel. No browser-session exchange.

set.title: Getting the job done
set.description:
A business chooses its channels: web pages, APIs described by OpenAPI or MCP, or its own conversational agent.

In the lab: a read-only endpoint for published TYPO3 text.

Sources: Sierra’s draft announcement and the draft specification.

match.header: Built on standards companies already run

set.header: Built on standards companies already run

set.title: Established standards
set.content:
Poppy builds on OAuth, JSON Web Tokens and HTTPS, with interaction channels described through OpenAPI or MCP. Teams can build on familiar infrastructure and add supported channels over time.

Sierra describes a shared integration for personal agents that industries can extend for their own tasks.

set.title: Complementary to UCP
set.content:
UCP covers commerce workflows such as product discovery, checkout and order management. Poppy covers agent identity, sessions and permitted access across a wider range of tasks.

Agent Nexus runs both side by side. Compare the protocols in the UCP demo.

set.header: Keep the personal agent’s work durable
set.subheadline: A durable personal agent calls the TYPO3 Lab knowledge API through Poppy. Its session state survives between tool calls.

set.bodytext:
Pi Durable provides the runtime for a personal agent whose conversations and tool work need to survive interruptions. Poppy provides the interface to the company. TYPO3 provides the editable, published knowledge.

In our example, a Pi tool discovers TYPO3 Lab, verifies its issuer, starts a signed-out session and reads the Poppy explanation. The tool returns only the published answer and its source URL to the model. Signing keys, DPoP keys and Session Tokens stay in private durable storage.

The example includes a protocol client and a Cloudflare Agents SDK PiHarness integration. Its transport is tested against TYPO3 locally. Cloudflare deployment and live model inference require a configured caller origin and authenticated application routing.

set.subheadline: Pi Durable keeps the agent’s work. Poppy verifies the request. TYPO3 supplies the published answer and its source.

set.title: Pi Durable
set.description:
The personal agent keeps its conversation, tool work and private protocol state in durable storage. It can resume after an interruption and renew its guest session when necessary.

Signing keys, DPoP keys and tokens stay private. Explore the Pi Durable source example.

You: What does TYPO3 Lab say about Poppy, and how does Pi Durable fit?

Expected assistant response: The lab offers verified guest sessions and a read-only API for its published explanations. Pi Durable runs the personal agent and preserves its work; Poppy carries the requests; TYPO3 owns the content. Sources: the Poppy and Pi Durable feature pages.

This is an example transcript, not a claim that a live model ran on this page. The included integration test runs the discovery, session, renewal and content requests against TYPO3.

set.title: Poppy help: install, connect and test
set.seo_title: Poppy help: install, connect and test | TYPO3 Lab
set.description: Install the TYPO3 Poppy extension, register a personal agent, edit published answers and diagnose protocol errors.

set.subheadline: Install the extension, connect a registered agent and keep the lab’s explanation current in TYPO3.

set.bodytext:
Require webconsulting/typo3-poppy from our GitLab repository, run TYPO3 extension setup and flush caches. Enable poppy.enabled on the domain’s canonical root site. The discovery file belongs at /.well-known/poppy.json, not under a language or site path.

Configure the organisation name, exact allowed client metadata URLs and topic sources in the site’s poppy configuration. A source selects one public page slug and one text-section heading. The extension README contains the full configuration.

1. Open Agent Nexus → Poppy in the TYPO3 Page module.
  2. Edit the normal text element headed “What TYPO3 Lab says”.
  3. Publish your change using the normal TYPO3 workflow.
  4. Call the knowledge API again. It reads the current published record.

The Pi Durable page has its own answer under the same heading. Hidden, scheduled, workspace-only, group-protected and x402-gated records are not returned. The first release serves English source records.

1. Install the locked dependencies in Examples/pi-durable.
  2. Set the public HTTPS TYPO3 origin, caller origin and Workers AI model.
  3. Deploy the Worker in your Cloudflare account and register its /agent.json URL in the TYPO3 site configuration.
  4. Connect LabAssistant.ask through your application’s authenticated, user-scoped routing.
  5. Ask the agent to read the Poppy and Pi Durable topics.

The example Worker publishes client metadata and public signing keys. Private keys and Session Tokens remain in durable storage. Its generic agent routes are not publicly exposed.

• invalid_client: check the exact allowlist URL, public metadata, same-host HTTPS JWKS, signing algorithm and assertion audience.
  • invalid_grant: create fresh independent assertions. Check expiry, clock and unique assertion IDs.
  • invalid_dpop_proof: sign the current HTTP method and URL without query or fragment. Use the bound key and the token hash. Never reuse a proof.
  • invalid_session: start a new guest session. Do not reuse another agent’s or user’s session ID.
  • not_found: check the configured topic, source slug, exact section heading and publication permissions.
  • rate_limited: wait for the response’s Retry-After interval.

Guest sessions grant no account scopes. Requests for account scopes are rejected. Tokens belong in the Authorization header.

Test Poppy in your browser: choose a topic, ask the lab, renew the session and test replay protection. Expand “See the requests” to inspect HTTP outcomes. The playground uses the same published CMS content as external personal agents.

The extension’s Build/Scripts/runTests.sh runs the PHP unit suite and syntax checks. The Pi Durable example has transport tests, TypeScript checks and a Worker dry build. The lab’s Build/Scripts/test-poppy.sh runs authenticated requests against DDEV, verifies renewal and replay rejection, then removes its temporary test identity.

Back to the feature · Pi Durable example · Source and README

set.header: Six agent protocols running on TYPO3
set.bodytext:
Explore how a personal agent identifies itself, builds interfaces, streams its work, delegates tasks and prepares purchases. Agent Nexus brings six protocols together in one field guide: A2UI, AG-UI, A2A, UCP, AP2 and Poppy.

Choose a protocol below, read how it works and try its demo. The first five run sandbox workflows; Poppy makes verified, read-only requests to published TYPO3 knowledge. Nothing is charged or sent to another person.

Identity and access → Poppy. Start here to understand how a site recognises a personal agent. Continue to A2UI for interfaces, AG-UI for streaming and approvals, A2A for delegated tasks, UCP for checkout and AP2 for payment authorisation.

Use the shared playground to compare the five embedded demos, or open the Poppy playground to discover the lab, start a session and request a sourced explanation. The Pi Durable example shows how the calling agent can preserve its work.

Try A2UI, AG-UI, A2A, UCP and AP2 in the five embedded demos below. Each uses its own endpoint. For identity and access, open the Poppy playground: discover the lab, start a verified guest session, read published knowledge, renew the session and test replay rejection.

match.header: Poppy — identify the agent and read published knowledge

set.header: Poppy — identify the agent and read published knowledge

Agent Nexus is a field guide to six protocols. Its bundled extension implements A2UI, AG-UI, A2A, UCP and AP2; the independent TYPO3 Poppy extension adds personal-agent identity and guest access. Each protocol has an explanation and a working demo.
